featuredProjects.name: ExamGuard
featuredProjects.shortDescription: Examination management and identity verification for secure exam entry.
featuredProjects.description: Connects registrations, hall tickets, seating, attendance, invigilation, and browser-based identity verification into one auditable examination workflow. Verification evidence is persisted while rules and human review remain responsible for the final decision.
featuredProjects.problem: Traditional exam entry relies on manual hall-ticket checks and visual ID verification by invigilators, which is slow, error-prone, vulnerable to impersonation (proxy candidates), and produces no auditable verification trail.
featuredProjects.architecture: Modular service architecture combining a Next.js operational dashboard, Python/FastAPI verification service, UniFace facial recognition pipeline with liveness estimation, Cloudinary secure photo evidence store, and PostgreSQL for immutable decision auditing.
keyDecisions: Separated verification evidence generation from final review authority — algorithms score liveness and facial likeness, but configurable threshold rules and invigilators retain decision sovereignty.
Protected server-side facial embedding storage to prevent unauthorized biometric extraction.
Typed domain failure states (e.g. LOW_LIVENESS, POOR_LIGHTING, MISMATCH, SEAT_CONFLICT) with dedicated coordinator review queues.
Role-based granular access control for Exam Admin, Room Invigilator, Chief Superintendent, and System Auditor.
qaEvidence: 2,554 backend tests verifying role permissions, authentication tokens, ticket validation, and seating constraint algorithms.
Deterministic mock testing for webcam video capture and liveness detection fallbacks.
Rigorous integration tests verifying candidate registration, hall-ticket generation, attendance marking, and tamper-resistant audit logs.

featuredProjects.name: SubstiFlow
featuredProjects.shortDescription: Offline timetable generation and faculty-substitution management for college coordinators.
featuredProjects.description: Replaces spreadsheet-driven substitution work with a local desktop workflow: generate a timetable draft, validate hard constraints, review deterministic substitute recommendations, approve and lock assignments, then issue a revised timetable without mutating the master schedule.
featuredProjects.problem: Department coordinators face daily morning chaotic scrambles when faculty members call in sick. Manual timetable spreadsheets lead to classroom double-bookings, violation of maximum teaching hour constraints, and untracked substitution histories.
featuredProjects.architecture: Local-first Electron desktop application with React + TypeScript frontend, SQLite relational database, deterministic constraint-satisfaction engine, and atomic export pipelines.
keyDecisions: Pure local-first architecture ensuring coordinators can manage substitutions even when campus network or internet is down.
Deterministic substitute ranking engine evaluating hard constraints (no overlapping lectures, subject qualification, max daily workload) before soft preferences.
Immutable assignment locking: once an emergency substitution is coordinator-approved, the revised schedule is frozen and logged to prevent accidental overrides.
Separation of master schedule records from daily substitution deltas.
qaEvidence: Comprehensive unit and property-based tests in Vitest validating constraint solver edge cases (e.g. zero available faculty, cyclical conflicts).
Transactional SQLite rollback verification ensuring schedule mutations are never half-applied.
Export snapshot test suite verifying printed daily substitution slips and PDF schedules.

featuredProjects.name: Anomoly Chat
featuredProjects.shortDescription: Accountless peer-to-peer chat and document transfer between browsers.
featuredProjects.description: Creates temporary browser-to-browser rooms using WebRTC data channels. Messages and documents stay in memory, binary transfers are checked with SHA-256, and absolute expiry clears the session on schedule. It is privacy-focused, not an anonymity guarantee: peer IP exposure remains a WebRTC boundary.
featuredProjects.problem: Standard messaging platforms require phone numbers or email logins, persist full message histories on centralized servers, and subject private file transfers to cloud analysis.
featuredProjects.architecture: Peer-to-peer direct communication model using PeerJS for room signaling, direct WebRTC RTCDataChannels for transport, in-memory ephemeral state, and Web Crypto API for client-side SHA-256 integrity verification.
keyDecisions: Accountless design: No database, no user accounts, no message history persisted on any central server.
16 KiB chunked binary transmission for documents (up to 10 MiB) with real-time transfer progress and end-of-transfer SHA-256 hash validation.
Scheduled session self-destruction: Rooms automatically expire after a set duration, wiping all in-memory buffers.
Transparent security boundaries: Explicit disclosure that peer IP exposure remains a fundamental WebRTC peer-connection characteristic.
qaEvidence: Network disconnection and peer reconnection test scenarios over simulated high-latency connections.
Binary integrity tests comparing original files against 16 KiB chunk-reassembled files using SHA-256 digests.
Memory leak tests confirming browser garbage collection after session self-destruction.

featuredProjects.name: What's Not Up
featuredProjects.shortDescription: Local visual privacy controls for WhatsApp Web and Instagram.
featuredProjects.description: A Manifest V3 extension that visually hides sensitive content already rendered in supported sites. It uses layered DOM detection, independent privacy categories, reveal controls, and local settings without claiming encryption, network interception, or protection against screenshots.
featuredProjects.problem: Using messaging platforms like WhatsApp Web or Instagram in public libraries, classrooms, or office desks leaves private messages, contact names, and media visible to shoulder surfers.
featuredProjects.architecture: Chromium Manifest V3 browser extension utilizing dynamic MutationObservers, scoped CSS blur/obfuscation rules, event-driven reveal mechanisms, and local Chrome Storage.
keyDecisions: Decoupled privacy categories: Independent toggles for message text, sender names, media previews, and profile photos.
Resilient DOM detection: Layered selector strategy coupled with MutationObserver to reliably catch dynamic chat loads, infinite scrolling, and SPA navigation.
Instant Panic Lock shortcut: Single hotkey immediately re-engages maximum blur across all active tabs.
Zero external network telemetry: Manifest V3 declared with minimal permissions and zero external network calls.
qaEvidence: DOM mutation stress testing against dynamic infinite-scrolling WhatsApp Web chats.
Hover-reveal state transition tests ensuring clean unblur on hover and immediate re-blur on mouseout.
Permission audit ensuring no host permissions outside supported messaging domains.

featuredProjects.name: DSCASC AI
featuredProjects.shortDescription: Student guidance assistant for admissions, academics, placements, and campus services.
featuredProjects.description: An academic chatbot built around an explainable NLP pipeline: normalize the query, build TF-IDF vectors, rank with cosine similarity, and fall back below a confidence threshold instead of inventing an answer.
featuredProjects.problem: College students and prospective applicants frequently struggle to locate official answers regarding admissions, fees, syllabus, and placement schedules across dispersed circulars and PDF notices.
featuredProjects.architecture: Deterministic NLP pipeline embedded in Next.js/React, featuring text normalization, tokenization, TF-IDF vector modeling, and cosine similarity vector ranking.
keyDecisions: Deterministic explainability: Vector scores and similarity rankings are fully inspectable, eliminating black-box LLM hallucinations.
Custom normalization dictionary: Normalizes common college shorthand, course abbreviations (e.g. BCA, MCA, MBA), and frequent student typos.
Strict confidence fallbacks: Queries below a 0.45 similarity threshold gracefully trigger structured contact cards rather than guessing answers.
Zero ongoing API costs: Runs entirely client/server-side without third-party LLM inference dependencies.
qaEvidence: Comprehensive intent-matching test matrix covering 40+ curated academic categories.
Typo resilience tests evaluating accuracy across misspelled student queries.
Boundary evaluation of confidence thresholds ensuring invalid queries consistently trigger structured fallbacks.
